common.coming_soon_body: This section hasn't been built yet.

login.sub: Sign in with your Fablab Google account
login.footer: Staff sign in with Google. Customers sign in with the email they were invited on.
login.email_sub: Enter the email address your designer invited. We'll send you a one-click sign-in link.
login.email_error: Couldn't send the link — try again or contact your designer.
login.email_sent_body: We sent a one-click sign-in link to {email}. Open it on this device to view your project.
login.auth_failed: Sign-in didn't complete. This usually means the link expired or was opened in a different browser than the one that started it. Try signing in again.

action.resend_po_email_title: Re-send the BINDING PO letter to the vendor. Use when the original delivery failed or the vendor asks for another copy. Doesn't change PO status.

po_confirmation.title: Vendor confirmation
po_confirmation.awaiting_body: The §2 PO template asks the supplier to confirm acceptance in writing within 5 business days. Once you have that confirmation (email reply, signed PO, etc.), record it here.
po_confirmation.days_since_issue: {n, plural, =0 {Issued today.} =1 {1 day since issue.} other {# days since issue.}}
po_confirmation.notes_placeholder: E.g. "Reply from Jens on 3 Jun confirming PO as written; PDF in Drive".
po_confirmation.undo_confirm: Undo this confirmation? The PO returns to issued. The original audit row stays so you keep the history.

today.intake_empty: No open leads. New enquiries land here.
today.active_projects_empty_mine: No active projects assigned to you. Use Show: All to see the wider team's.
today.approvals_empty: No approvals waiting on the client.
today.pos_ready_heading: Commercial protection — POs ready to issue
today.pos_ready_empty: No POs are queued for issue — every commitment is either still being priced or already binding.
today.awaiting_confirmation_heading: Awaiting vendor confirmation — BINDING but not yet acknowledged
today.awaiting_confirmation_empty: Every issued PO has been confirmed by its vendor.
today.awaiting_confirmation_days: {n, plural, =0 {issued today} =1 {1 day since issue} other {# days since issue}}
today.risk_heading: Risk — projects on hold or in dispute
today.risk_empty: No projects on hold or in dispute.
today.recent_empty: Nothing's moved in the last 7 days.

coach_card.title: Coach
coach_card.subtitle: {count, plural, =1 {1 thing worth your attention} other {# things worth your attention}}

coach_dashboard.title: Project Coach
coach_dashboard.subtitle_quiet: Nothing worth nudging right now. The Coach checks the project's evidence health continuously and will surface findings here when they appear.
coach_dashboard.subtitle_active: {count, plural, =1 {1 open finding} other {# open findings}} — acknowledge what you've seen, resolve what's done, dismiss what doesn't apply.
coach_dashboard.empty_doctrine: All clear. The Coach has nothing to flag — keep doing what you're doing.

action.ack_title: Acknowledge — you've seen this. Stays in the dashboard until resolved.
action.resolve_title: Mark this resolved manually (the Coach auto-resolves when the underlying condition clears).
action.dismiss_title: Hide this — it doesn't apply to this project. Won't re-fire even if the rule matches again.

brief_no_signoff.observation: The customer hasn't signed off the brief yet.
brief_no_signoff.why: Without sign-off, scope drift can't be defended later — the brief is the contract.

brief_signoff_drifted.observation: The brief has been edited since the customer signed off.
brief_signoff_drifted.why: Their consent no longer matches the live brief. Ask them to re-sign before procurement moves on revised scope.

brief_unreplied_comments.observation: {count, plural, =1 {1 customer comment} other {# customer comments}} in the last 7 days without a Fablab reply.
brief_unreplied_comments.why: Unanswered comments become "Fablab didn't respond" later — keep the thread moving so the audit reads clean.

scope_no_approval.observation: No approved scope baseline on record.
scope_no_approval.why: Scope baseline is the commercial reference for chargeable vs change. Without it, every later question about "was this included?" gets harder.

approvals_stalled.observation: {count, plural, =1 {1 approval} other {# approvals}} sent over 7 days ago, no response yet.
approvals_stalled.why: Stalled approvals block procurement and erode customer momentum.

items_r3_violation.observation: {count, plural, =1 {1 item ordered} other {# items ordered}} without an approved Approval (R3 gate violation).
items_r3_violation.why: Per 00- §22, an approved Approval is the binding evidence behind a PO. Items past `ordered` without one expose margin and undermine the audit trail.

change_open.observation: {count, plural, =1 {1 open change order} other {# open change orders}} awaiting next step.
change_open.why: Change orders stuck in the pipeline are commercial risk — every day in `requested` or `priced` is work being done at uncertain chargeability.

delivery_stuck.observation: {count, plural, =1 {1 item in an exception state} other {# items in exception states}} (backorder / damaged / on hold).
delivery_stuck.why: Stuck items quietly become customer expectation-management problems. Each one needs a resolution path or a customer note.

handover_awaiting.observation: {count, plural, =1 {1 item installed} other {# items installed}} awaiting client sign-off.
handover_awaiting.why: Per 00- §22, written sign-off is the load-bearing artefact at this stage. Close them out to advance the project.

risk_supplier_open.observation: {count, plural, =1 {1 supplier risk} other {# supplier risks}} open in the register.
risk_supplier_open.why: Supplier risks belong in the next Work Evidence Summary so the customer sees what Fablab is actively managing.

time_missing_reason.observation: {count, plural, =1 {1 time entry} other {# time entries}} reportable but missing a commercial reason.
time_missing_reason.why: Without the reason, the hour is hidden in the next Work Evidence Summary — the customer sees a number without context.

time_chargeable_unreported.observation: {hours} chargeable hours ({count, plural, =1 {1 entry} other {# entries}}) not yet included in a customer report.
time_chargeable_unreported.why: Chargeable hours forgotten before reporting = lost billing. Generate the next Work Evidence Summary to roll them up.

time_goodwill.observation: {hours} hours of goodwill recorded in the last 14 days.
time_goodwill.why: Goodwill is a story to tell, not a cost to hide. Make sure your customer summary mentions what was done at our cost.

coach.row_cta_title: Document this work in the Project Coach
coach.step_stage_intro: Confirm what stage you're in and what work you're reviewing. The Coach uses this to surface the right prompts and to file the evidence note in the right category.
coach.field_task_placeholder: A short summary of the task or decision — e.g. "Sourcing replacement chair after Wong & Co stockout".
coach.step_work_intro: Pick the type(s) of work this evidence covers. Linking it to a specific entity (an item, a PO, a comment) makes the audit trail navigable later.
coach.field_source_id_placeholder: Paste the entity's UUID if you have it — otherwise leave blank.
coach.field_source_id_help: Pre-filled when the Coach is opened from a specific entity. Manual entry is for free-standing notes.
coach.step_why_intro: Why did this work matter? Pick from the controlled list, add your own framing, and write the customer-facing version that will land in the next Work Evidence Summary.
coach.field_custom_reason_placeholder: Use this if no chip captures what you mean.
coach.field_customer_visible_reason_placeholde: Plain language — the line the customer will see.
coach.field_customer_visible_reason_help: Pre-fills the customer summary on the final step.
coach.step_scope_intro: Classify the work against the agreed scope baseline. This is where doctrine matters — the choice you make here drives how the work shows up in reporting (and what gets billed).
coach.follow_up_change_body: This looks like change-order territory. After committing this note, open Change Control and log the change so the commercial impact is recorded before the work continues.
coach.follow_up_change_hint: Tip: the wizard doesn't create the change order automatically — you stay in control of the binding write.
coach.follow_up_goodwill_body: Goodwill is a story to tell, not a cost to hide. Make sure your customer summary explains what was done at our cost so it lands in the next Work Evidence Summary with context.
coach.step_output_intro: Review what gets committed. The internal note is the staff record; the customer summary is what the customer reads. Both lands; the time entry is optional.
coach.field_evidence_category_help: Drives the section of the Work Evidence Summary this note appears under.
coach.field_customer_summary_placeholder: The plain-English line the customer will read.
coach.field_customer_summary_help: If empty, this entry won't show in the customer's report — only in the internal audit.
coach.field_include_in_report: Include in the next Work Evidence Summary
coach.field_also_create_time_entry: Also log a time entry from this work
coach.field_also_create_time_entry_help: Saves a step — the time entry is pre-filled with the commercial reason, customer summary, and chargeability you set above.

chargeability_explainer.included: Within the agreed scope baseline. Hours are part of the fixed engagement.
chargeability_explainer.chargeable: Additional billable project work — sits outside the fixed scope but inside the agreed engagement.
chargeability_explainer.change: Change-order territory. After this commits, open Change Control to log the binding change.
chargeability_explainer.out_of_scope_approval_needed: Outside the agreed scope. Customer approval (or a change order) is needed before billing.
chargeability_explainer.goodwill: Non-billable. Included at our cost — make sure the customer summary explains the value done on their behalf.
chargeability_explainer.internal_admin: Internal work. Never shown to the customer.
chargeability_explainer.rework_fablab: Rework caused by us. Non-billable; logged for honest internal accounting.
chargeability_explainer.rework_customer: Rework caused by a customer change. Usually chargeable via change order.
chargeability_explainer.rework_supplier: Rework caused by supplier issue. Usually chargeable to the supplier.

time.title: Time entries
time.subtitle: Your hours, grouped by week. The Coach prompt nudges any entry where there's a raw note but no commercial reason — that's what turns hours into the kind of story a customer can read.
time.signin_required: Sign in to view your time entries.
time.no_projects: No projects yet — log time once a project has been created.
time.empty_doctrine: No entries in the last 90 days. Use "+ Log time" to add your first.
time.delete_confirm: Delete this time entry? This can't be undone.
time.field_note_placeholder: A line or two — what you actually did. The detail.
time.field_commercial_reason_placeholder: Why this work mattered for the project — pick a chip or write your own.
time.field_customer_summary_placeholder: The line a customer will see in the next Work Evidence Summary.
time.field_customer_summary_help: Plain language. Imagine the customer reading it without context.
time.field_reportable_help: Include in the next Work Evidence Summary
time.field_non_chargeable_reason_placeholder: Required for audit when the work isn't billed to the customer.

coach.missing_reason_body: Without it, this hour will be hidden in the next Work Evidence Summary — the customer sees a number without context.

reporting.title: Reporting
reporting.subtitle: Portfolio-level view across every active project. The per-project reporting view lives on each project's Element List tab.

section_empty.risks: No open risks across the portfolio.
section_empty.change_orders: No open change orders across the portfolio.

reporting.deep_dive_intro: For row-level detail per project, jump into the entity pages.

risk.subtitle: Open risks first, sorted by score. Naming and owning a risk is half the mitigation.
risk.empty_doctrine: No risks logged yet. The register stays open across the project lifecycle — log anything that could cost time, money, scope, or reputation if it materialised.
risk.field_title_placeholder: E.g. "Supplier may miss the H&M deadline"
risk.field_description_placeholder: What could happen, what triggers it.
risk.field_mitigation_action_placeholder: How will we reduce the likelihood or impact?
risk.mitigation_empty: No mitigation plan yet. Add one to move this risk into mitigation_planned.
risk.residual_intro: Score the risk's residual likelihood and impact after the mitigation lands.
risk.accept_intro: Accepting a risk records that we chose not to mitigate it — usually because cost of mitigation exceeds the expected exposure. The reason is required for audit.
risk.accept_note_placeholder: Reason for accepting — what we considered vs the cost of mitigation.

handover.subtitle: Sign off each installed item with the client. Per 00- §22, written sign-off is the load-bearing artefact at this stage — when every item carries it, the project is ready to advance to Handover.
handover.empty_doctrine: No items at handover yet. Items appear here once they reach 'installed' in the Delivery view. Sign each one off with the client to close the project.
handover.progress_complete: Every installed item has been signed off — this project is ready for the Handover stage advancement.
handover.signoff_note_placeholder: Optional — witness, client name, condition notes.
handover.snag_note_placeholder: Required — what's wrong, what's the remedy?
handover.unsign_confirm: Undo the sign-off on this item? Item goes back to 'installed'. The signed_off_at date is cleared but the audit notes stay.

section_sub.awaiting: Installed but not yet signed off by the client
section_sub.snags: Issues raised at handover — drop back into Delivery exceptions

delivery.subtitle: Items move ordered → in production → ready → shipped → received → installed. Exceptions (on hold / backorder / damaged / substituted / cancelled) are first-class so nothing's invisible.
delivery.empty_doctrine: No items in the delivery pipeline yet. Items appear here once their PO is issued and they leave the design phase. Status begins at 'ordered' and progresses to 'installed' before the Handover module takes over.
delivery.advance_title: Advance this item to the next state
delivery.exception_title: Mark an exception (on hold, damaged, backorder etc.)
delivery.exception_note_placeholder: Short note for audit — what happened, what's blocking?

section_sub.ordered: PO issued, vendor working on it
section_sub.installed: Placed and ready for client sign-off (Handover)

change_order.subtitle: Every change after Brief sign-off must be recorded, priced, and approved before it's implemented. This is where that audit lives.
change_order.empty_doctrine: No change orders on this project yet. Once the Brief is signed off, any change to scope / cost / time / supplier that comes up should be logged here so it can be priced and re-approved before it becomes work.
change_order.withdraw_reason_placeholder: A short reason for withdrawal — kept on the row for audit.

confirm.review: Move this change order into Under review so it's clear someone owns scoping the impact?
confirm.send: Send this change order for client approval? A draft approval will be created — open it in the Approvals tab to finalise the approver details and send the email.
confirm.decision: Record the client's written response to this change order.
confirm.implement: Mark this change order as implemented? Use this once the change has actually landed on items / POs / scope. The timestamp stays on the row as evidence.
confirm.close: Close this change order? Use this only when implementation is fully complete and no follow-up is expected.
confirm.withdraw: Withdraw this change order? The row stays in the audit trail; the status flips to withdrawn so it stops appearing on Today's queue.

decision.reason_optional: Optional note from the client / conditions of approval

change_order_wizard.title: + New change order
change_order_wizard.field_title_placeholder: E.g. Switch sofa from Wong & Co to Massproductions
change_order_wizard.field_title_help: What's changing, in 5–10 words. The full description lives in step 2.
change_order_wizard.field_requested_by_external_placeholder: E.g. Marit Solem at Hotel Marin
change_order_wizard.field_reason_placeholder: Why is this change being asked for?
change_order_wizard.field_reason_help: Channeling the change back to its root motivates the right approval question downstream.
change_order_wizard.field_description_placeholder: What specifically changes — items, scope, materials, vendor, dates. Enough that someone reading later (or the client) understands without context.
change_order_wizard.field_cost_impact_help: Net cost delta in the project's currency. Leave blank if you still need to scope it — the CO will sit at Requested until you price it.
change_order_wizard.field_time_impact_help: Positive for delay, negative for time saved.
change_order_wizard.impact_intro: Estimate as best you can today. You can refine before sending for client approval.
change_order_wizard.review_intro: One last check before this lands on the audit trail.
change_order_wizard.review_starts_priced: This change order will be created at status Priced and is ready to send for client approval.
change_order_wizard.review_starts_requested: No cost impact yet — this change order will be created at Requested. Add a cost impact on the detail page before sending it for approval.

implication.design_advisory_only: Advisory engagement. Client contracts directly with suppliers and contractors. Fablab's liability is limited to advice quality.
implication.design_and_specification: Design + specification deliverables. Fablab does not procure. Liability limited to specification accuracy.
implication.procurement_support: Coordination role only. Client contracts directly with suppliers. Fablab's commitment is administrative.
implication.procurement_and_resale: Fablab owns the goods on this project. Required: PO in Fablab's name, transport insurance, product liability cover. Margin and landed cost monitoring active.
implication.supplier_coordination: Fablab coordinates suppliers but does not contract directly. Check freight insurance arrangements.
implication.delivery_coordination: Fablab manages delivery flow. Confirm freight insurance is in place before any cross-border shipment.
implication.installation_coordination: Fablab manages site install. Site insurance applies. Snag list and handover sign-off required.
implication.full_project_control: Full E&O, professional liability, transport, product, and site insurance coverage required. All approval gates active. Maximum commercial exposure.

lead.new_sub: Capture an enquiry — fill what you know, return to complete the rest.
lead.new_helper: Required fields are marked with *. The 16 required fields (per Rule R1) must all be filled before this lead can be converted to a project.
lead.intake_rule: Rule R1: no Project until intake is complete.
lead.miss_helper: The server refuses conversion until every required field is filled. This is the §2 intake gate, enforced both in the form and in the server action.
lead.already_converted: This lead has been converted to a project.

scope.empty: No scope versions yet. Start the guided wizard to draft v1 — it walks through the 15 structured scope fields from §4 of the Fablab best-practice guide.
scope.empty_blurb: Get the scope written down. Procurement is blocked (Rule R2) until at least one version is approved.
scope.next_steps_body: no version has been approved yet. The Scope gate stays in-progress (and procurement stays blocked) until an Approval with target = Scope baseline reaches approved status.

approval.empty: No approvals yet. Request your first approval to formalise a decision in writing — the Approval entity is what proves something has been agreed (§22 Q8).
approval.tab_footer: Approvals are the legal substance of the project. Rule R3 (no order without an approved item) and R5 (no verbal approval as final) are enforced via this register.
approval.new_helper: An Approval is the explicit, traceable record that something has been agreed. The legal substance — what's being approved, at what price, with what consequences — is captured here so it can be cited later.
approval.new_footer: Saves as Draft. Send from the detail screen to dispatch to the approver.
approval.subject: Subject
approval.subject_placeholder: e.g. Approve specification for Soriana lounge chair × 2
approval.description_placeholder: Spell out what is being approved — items, prices, terms, conditions.
approval.consequence_placeholder: What happens on approval — e.g. PO will be issued within 5 days, item will be specified for inclusion in the FF&E schedule, etc.

banner.draft_body: This approval is in draft state. Nothing has been communicated to the approver. Send it from the action panel to formally request a response.
banner.sent: Sent for client approval — awaiting response
banner.sent_body: The approver has been notified via the chosen channel. Until they respond, no order may be placed against the underlying target. Log their response below when received.
banner.approved: Approved — proof of agreement on file
banner.approved_body: The client has approved. The underlying target (item / PO / scope) is now cleared for the next stage. This approval is part of the §22 Q8 audit trail.
banner.conditions: Approved with conditions — conditions must be met
banner.conditions_body: The client has approved subject to specific conditions. Read them carefully before proceeding. The conditions are part of the approval record.
banner.rejected_body: The client did not approve. The underlying target cannot be ordered or progressed. Revise and submit a new approval request, or raise a Change Order.
banner.expired: Expired — approval was not actioned in time
banner.expired_body: The Valid Until date passed without a response. Treat as unanswered. Request a new approval before proceeding.
banner.superseded: Superseded — replaced by a newer approval
banner.superseded_body: This approval was replaced by a subsequent one. The newer record is canonical. Kept here for audit.

approval.conditions_placeholder: What conditions did the client attach?

vendor.empty: No vendors yet. Add a vendor to start receiving quotes.
vendor.new_sub: Capture a supplier, fabricator, contractor, or the in-house workshop.
vendor.name: Name
vendor.internal_helper: This vendor is the in-house workshop

package.empty: No packages yet. Create one to start specifying items — packages group items procurementally (by room, category, trade, or phase).
package.name: Name

kind_help.room: All items installed in one physical space. Reach for Room when decisions and budget track per room — typical for residential, hospitality and retail fit-outs.
kind_help.category: All items of one product type across the whole project. Reach for Category when you’re sourcing one category from a single specialist — e.g. all lighting from one supplier.
kind_help.trade: All items the same specialist discipline delivers or installs (joinery, electrical, glazing, painting, etc.). Reach for Trade on construction-led projects where bid packages go out to trade contractors.
kind_help.phase: All items delivered or installed together in one stage. Reach for Phase when the project ships in waves — e.g. Phase 1 install lands before Phase 2 design is complete.

package.intro: Packages group items so you can manage them together. You can mix grouping types within the same project — e.g. one "Hotel lobby FF&E" (Room) plus one "All joinery" (Trade) plus one "Phase 1 install" (Phase).

item.new_sub: Add a sourced or bespoke item to a package. You can flesh out details later.
item.name: Name
item.no_quotes: No quotes yet. Add this item to an RFQ to start collecting prices.

rfq.empty: No RFQs yet. Create one to invite vendors to quote against specified items.
rfq.new_sub: Select items + invited vendors. Save as draft, then send to dispatch the RFQ as a stage-labelled communication.
rfq.new_footer: Saved RFQs start as Draft. Send from the detail screen to create pending Quote rows for each vendor × item.
rfq.banner_label: Request for Quotation — not an order
rfq.banner_body: RFQs are price inquiries with a legal disclaimer. Selecting a winning quote signals intent but does not create an order. Only a Purchase Order with status Issued is binding (Rule R3).
rfq.title: Title
rfq.no_items: No items in `specified` status. Create items on the Packages tab first.
rfq.no_vendors: No vendors registered. Add vendors from the Vendors page first.
rfq.draft_helper: This RFQ is still in draft. Click Send RFQ to dispatch it to the invited vendors and create pending Quote rows.

po.empty: No POs yet. Once you have winning quotes from a vendor, draft a PO to commit.
po.new_sub: Drafts a PO covering this project's winning quotes from one vendor.
po.new_footer: PO starts as Draft. From the detail screen, the Issue button is gated by Rule R3 — every line item needs an approved Approval first.
po.no_candidates_body: No vendor has winning quotes ready for a PO. Select winning quotes on the RFQs tab first.
po.no_approval_yet: — Not selected (PO cannot be issued without one)
po.authorising_approval_helper: The Approval that authorises this PO. Rule R3 requires this before issuance.

banner.draft_body: This PO is in draft form. The vendor has not received it and no commitment exists. The Issue button is gated by Rule R3 — every line item must have an approved Approval.
banner.review_body: Internal review before vendor dispatch. Vendor will not see this PO until Issued.
banner.issued_body: This Purchase Order has been issued to the vendor. Both parties are committed. Goods/services to be supplied as specified.
banner.confirmed_body: The vendor has acknowledged the order. Production / fulfilment is now active.
banner.partial_body: Some line items have been delivered; others are still outstanding.
banner.fulfilled_body: All line items delivered. PO complete.

po.gate_missing_items: {count} line item(s) lack a client-approved Approval.
po.gate_needs_auth_approval: This PO has no authorising Approval. Link one in the PO details before issuing.
po.no_authorising_approval: No authorising Approval linked — R3 requires one.
po.issue_and_send_ok: PO issued and emailed to the vendor.
po.issue_ok_email_failed: PO issued but email could not be sent:
po.resend_ok: PO email re-sent to the vendor.

finance.cross_sub: Cross-project receivables, mirrored from Poweroffice. The Controller doesn't generate invoices — it tracks them for project P&L visibility.
finance.empty: No invoices logged yet. When you raise an invoice in Poweroffice, log it here to keep project P&L visibility.
finance.pipeline_title: Billing triggers fired — invoice in Poweroffice
finance.pipeline_helper: These project events have fired billing triggers. Raise the corresponding invoice in Poweroffice, then log it here.

invoice.new_sub: Record an invoice that has been raised in Poweroffice. The Controller mirrors it for project P&L; Poweroffice remains the source of truth.
invoice.new_footer: Saves as Draft. Mark as Issued once the invoice has been raised in Poweroffice.
invoice.due_helper: Defaults to issue date + {days} days (client payment terms)

banner.draft: Draft — log when raised in Poweroffice
banner.draft_body: This invoice record is in draft. Mark as Issued once the corresponding invoice has been raised in Poweroffice.
banner.issued_body: Invoice logged. Mark as Sent once delivered to the client. Payment will be tracked from Poweroffice (or recorded manually below).
banner.sent_body: Client has been notified. Record payment when received (or sync from Poweroffice when API integration lands).
banner.partial_body: Some amount received. Outstanding balance still due.
banner.overdue_body: The due date has passed without full payment. Follow up with the client or check Poweroffice for status.
banner.void_body: This invoice has been voided and is excluded from financial rollups.

elementList.title: Element List
elementList.bannerInternal: Internal view — shows cost prices, margins and markup. Never share outside Fablab.
elementList.bannerCustomer: Customer view — cost prices and margins are masked at the database query level.
elementList.bannerSupplier: Supplier view — filtered to this supplier's items only; no margin or customer pricing shown.
elementList.empty: No items in this project yet. Add items to a package to start the Element List.
elementList.cascadeNote: Derived columns are computed at render time from unit cost × quantity × margin %, then discount and VAT. Storing the result risks staleness when discount or VAT change.

brief.next_role: Confirm the Fablab role on the lead — this carries through to the project.
brief.next_approval: Request a Scope-target approval and mark it approved to complete the Brief.

scope.next_approve: Create a Scope version and get it approved.

items.next_create: Add at least one Item via Packages.
items.next_quote: Record quotes for the remaining items so every item has cost state at least Quoted.

procurement.next_items: All items must reach Quoted cost state first.
procurement.next_issue: Issue at least one Purchase Order to advance Procurement.

delivery.next_procurement: Issue at least one PO first.
delivery.next_track: Track items through Ordered → Shipped → Received.

handover.next_delivery: All items must be Received before Handover begins.
handover.next_signoff: Sign off remaining items to complete Handover.

items_wizard.title: + Add item (guided)
items_wizard.where_helper: Items live inside packages — pick the one this item belongs to, or create a new package first.
items_wizard.specification_helper: All optional. Fill in what you know now; you can edit later.
items_wizard.review_helper: Review and create — or use the secondary button to immediately start another item in the same package.

rfq_wizard.title: + New RFQ (guided)
rfq_wizard.basics_helper: Give the RFQ a clear title and a realistic response deadline. Vendors see both.
rfq_wizard.title_placeholder: e.g. Living room lighting RFQ — May 2026
rfq_wizard.items_helper: Pick the items vendors should quote on. Only items in `specified` status are shown.
rfq_wizard.no_items: No items in `specified` status. Create items on the Items step first.
rfq_wizard.vendors_helper: Vendors whose categories match the selected items appear under "Matched".
rfq_wizard.no_vendors: No active vendors. Add vendors from the Vendors page first.
rfq_wizard.review_helper: Review the RFQ before creating. Tick "Send now" to dispatch it immediately and open Quote rows for each vendor × item.
rfq_wizard.send_now_on: The RFQ will be created and immediately marked as sent — pending Quote rows are created for every vendor × item combination.
rfq_wizard.send_now_off: The RFQ will be saved as a draft. You can send it later from the RFQ detail page.
rfq_wizard.body_helper: A draft RFQ letter has been generated for you from the Fablab specimen (per 20-doc-templates-best-practice.md, adapted for multi-supplier RFQ). Edit freely — the placeholders in [square brackets] are substituted per recipient at send time.
rfq_wizard.body_placeholders_note: Placeholders in [brackets] are filled per vendor at send time: [supplier contact name], [your name], [your email].

rfq_attachments.title: Attachments
rfq_attachments.empty: No attachments. Add specifications, drawings, or reference PDFs that will go out with the email.
rfq_attachments.too_large: {name} is over the {max} limit and was not uploaded.

po_wizard.title: + New PO (guided)
po_wizard.vendor_helper: Only vendors with at least one winning quote on this project — and items not already on a non-cancelled PO — appear here.
po_wizard.no_candidates: No vendors have winning quotes ready to order on this project. Select winning quotes on the RFQs tab first.
po_wizard.pick_vendor_first: Pick a vendor on step 1 first.
po_wizard.lines_helper: These lines are auto-generated from the vendor’s winning quotes. Edit quantities or unit costs later on the PO detail page if needed.
po_wizard.delivery_helper: Delivery, freight, and customs terms travel with the PO when it is issued and bind both parties.
po_wizard.authorisation_helper: Rule R3 requires every PO to cite the approved Approval that authorises it. Pick one below.
po_wizard.no_approvals_yet: There are no approved Approvals on this project yet, so a PO cannot be issued (R3 gate). Create and approve an Approval first.
po_wizard.approval_r3_note: Per Rule R3 (00- §22), no PO may be issued without an approved authorising Approval on file. This link is recorded permanently on the PO.
po_wizard.review_helper: Review the PO and create it as a DRAFT. Issuing the PO (which is BINDING) is a separate, gated action on the PO detail page.
po_wizard.draft_only_body: This wizard creates an unissued draft. The vendor will not receive it and no commitment exists until you click "Issue" on the detail page — which is BINDING.

po_attachments.title: Attachments
po_attachments.empty: No attachments. Add drawings, specifications, or supplementary terms that will go out with the PO.
po_attachments.too_large: {name} is over the {max} limit and was not uploaded.

scope_wizard.title: + New scope version (guided)
scope_wizard.review_intro: {filled} of {total} fields filled. Empty fields are allowed in the draft — but the more you fill, the less room for "we never agreed that" later.
scope_wizard.draft_only_body: This creates an unapproved draft. Per Rule R2 (00- §4), procurement cannot begin until a version reaches "approved" status — request an Approval with target = Scope baseline from the Approvals tab once you’re ready.
scope_wizard.areas_intro: Start by naming WHAT this scope covers: which parts of the property, which rooms or zones. Boundaries make the rest of the scope easier to write.
scope_wizard.h_project_areas: A short paragraph describing the overall area(s) the project covers — e.g. "Ground floor and mezzanine of the new wing".
scope_wizard.e_project_areas: e.g. Ground floor lobby, bar, restaurant, and ground-floor guest amenities.
scope_wizard.h_rooms_zones: The specific spaces within the project areas. List each one. These become the package "rooms" later.
scope_wizard.e_rooms_zones:
Reception
Lobby seating
Bar
Restaurant
Guest WCs
scope_wizard.services_intro: 00- §4 frames this as the most-disputed scope axis. List exactly what Fablab is doing AND exactly what Fablab is not doing — the second list is the one that prevents change-order arguments later.
scope_wizard.h_included: Every discipline / activity Fablab is responsible for under this scope. Be specific — "design" is too vague; "concept design, design development, FF&E specification" is workable.
scope_wizard.e_included:
Concept design
Design development
FF&E specification
Procurement coordination
Installation supervision
scope_wizard.h_excluded: Things that COULD be assumed in scope but are not. This is the change-order-prevention list — write it generously.
scope_wizard.e_excluded:
Structural design
M&E engineering
Fire engineering
Planning permission application
Property survey
Kitchen equipment specification
scope_wizard.deliverables_intro: What does Fablab hand over at the end? Deliverables are the THINGS the client receives; design outputs are the formal documents/files within those deliverables.
scope_wizard.h_deliverables: What the client gets at the end (or at each stage). Concrete nouns — drawings, packs, lists, installed rooms.
scope_wizard.e_deliverables:
Concept presentation
FF&E schedule
Installed rooms ready for occupancy
Operations & maintenance pack
scope_wizard.h_design_outputs: The formal design artefacts within the deliverables — drawings, schedules, specifications, sample boards.
scope_wizard.e_design_outputs:
Concept boards
General arrangement drawings 1:50
FF&E schedule (Excel + PDF)
Material sample board
scope_wizard.responsibilities_intro: Who is on the hook for what. 00- §11 treats supplier and procurement clarity as essential — and explicit client responsibilities prevent surprise dependencies.
scope_wizard.h_procurement_resp: What does Fablab procure on this project — and crucially, what does the client procure directly? Be precise.
scope_wizard.h_supplier_coord: For items the client procures directly, does Fablab still coordinate the supplier (issue RFQs, check submittals, manage delivery)? Specify.
scope_wizard.h_client_resp: What does the client commit to provide — site access, approvals within X days, builder coordination, etc. Their delays become legitimate cost-and-time recoveries when listed here.
scope_wizard.expectations_intro: The "what we’re assuming" section. If reality differs from any of these once the project is underway, it’s a legitimate Change Order trigger.
scope_wizard.h_site_visits: How many site visits are included? Day visits or overnight? Geographic limit? Beyond this is an additional cost line.
scope_wizard.h_meetings: How many design/review/install meetings are included? In person or remote? With whom (designer + client, designer + builder, full team)?
scope_wizard.h_timeline: The schedule Fablab is signing up to deliver against — handover dates, approval turnaround Fablab expects from the client, builder readiness.
scope_wizard.h_budget: The budget envelope this scope is sized for. Includes currency, exchange-rate assumptions for imports, and any cost-escalation contingency.
scope_wizard.gates_intro: 00- §22 ("approval is the contract") wants every commit point named up-front. The gates list anchors when written approval is required; dependencies are external constraints Fablab needs the client to manage.
scope_wizard.h_approval_gates: Every point at which written client approval is required before Fablab proceeds. List them so the cadence of approvals is agreed at scope time, not negotiated later.
scope_wizard.e_approval_gates:
Concept sign-off
Design development sign-off
FF&E specification sign-off
Procurement budget sign-off
Final installation sign-off
scope_wizard.h_known_deps: External constraints that affect Fablab’s ability to deliver — builder schedule, permissions, client decisions, imported-goods lead times. List what you’re depending on.

brief.subtitle: The Brief gate needs three things: project description filled, Fablab role confirmed, and at least one approved scope-target Approval (Phase 2).

brief_wizard.title: Review brief (guided)
brief_wizard.intake_intro: These are the 16 intake fields from the lead this project was converted from (00- §2). They’re read-only here — use them as context for writing the brief on the next step. Edits to the original intake belong on the lead, not the project.
brief_wizard.no_lead_context: No originating lead is linked to this project — intake context is not available. You can still edit description and role in the next step.
brief_wizard.edit_intro: The project description is the brief. It seeds from the lead’s desired outcome (usually a single sentence) — expand it here into the working brief: what the project is, the design intent, the constraints, the stakeholders, anything a new team member should know on day one.
brief_wizard.desc_placeholder: A few paragraphs describing the project, design intent, key constraints, and stakeholders.
brief_wizard.desc_helper: Aim for something a new designer could read in 5 minutes and understand the engagement. The lead intake fields above give you the supporting facts.
brief_wizard.gate_intro: Phase 2’s Brief gate needs all three of these to flip ✓. The third — the approved scope-target Approval — is a separate Approvals action and is read here from the live gate state.
brief_wizard.scope_pending_body: Draft a scope version (the Scope tab) and request an Approval with target = Scope baseline. Once that approval reaches approved, the Brief gate flips to done.
brief_wizard.all_ok: ✓ All three Brief gate criteria met. Saving will persist the description and role; the Brief gate will read as done on the next refresh.
brief_wizard.save_anyway: You can still save description + role now. The Brief gate will flip to done once the missing criterion above is satisfied.

portal.welcome_sub: These are the projects you have access to. Click one to view its brief and the current state of work.
portal.welcome_attention: {n, plural, =1 {One project} other {# projects}} need your attention — they're listed first.
portal.welcome_all_caught_up: You're caught up on every project — all signed off on the current brief.
portal.no_projects: You haven't been invited to any projects yet. Your designer at Fablab will invite you once your project's brief is ready to share.
portal.brief_empty: Your designer is still writing the brief. Check back shortly.
portal.intake_heading: What we captured from the initial conversation
portal.intake_sub: This is what your designer noted during intake. If anything's wrong or missing, you'll be able to comment on it once that feature is enabled (coming next).
portal.uploads_body: Mood boards, inspiration photos, existing site plans, samples — anything that helps the designer see what you mean.
portal.comments_body: Add notes against any part of the brief. Corrections, clarifications, missing context — anything you want recorded.
portal.signoff_body: When the brief reflects what you want, sign off to formally confirm it. This becomes the agreed starting point.

customer_portal.activity_empty: Nobody on the client side has been invited yet. Invite the customer once the brief is in good enough shape for them to review.
customer_portal.invite_body: Sends a magic-link email so the customer can view this project's brief, upload references, comment, and sign off. They never see other projects unless you invite them separately.
customer_portal.invite_note_placeholder: E.g. "Hi Marit — please have a read and tell us if anything's missing. We'd like your sign-off by Friday."
customer_portal.revoke_confirm: Revoke this customer's access? They'll no longer be able to view the project. The audit row is kept.

portal_uploads.title: References you've shared
portal_uploads.help: Upload mood boards, inspiration photos, existing plans, sample images — anything that helps your designer see what you mean. Up to 5 MB per file.
portal_uploads.confirm_delete: Remove this file? Your designer will no longer see it.
portal_uploads.delete_failed: Couldn't remove the file. Try again or refresh the page.
portal_uploads.download_failed: Couldn't open the file. Try again in a moment.
portal_uploads.too_large: {name} is larger than {max}. Please reduce the file size and try again.

customer_uploads_staff.title: Files from the customer
customer_uploads_staff.help: References the customer has shared from the portal. Click a filename to download.
customer_uploads_staff.empty: The customer hasn't uploaded anything yet.

brief_signoff.title: Sign off the brief
brief_signoff.intro: When this brief reflects what you want, sign off below to make that confirmation part of the project record. This is the moment Fablab can plan, source, and commit on the basis of an agreed brief.
brief_signoff.confirm_body: By signing off, you confirm in writing that the brief above — the description, the Fablab role, and the captured intake — reflects your intent for the project.
brief_signoff.confirm_legal: Your name, the timestamp, and a frozen copy of the brief at this moment are recorded as evidence. You can comment or upload further references at any time; if the brief itself changes substantively, your designer will ask you to sign off again.
brief_signoff.signed_body: Fablab now treats this brief as the agreed starting point for the project. You can still comment, upload, or talk to your designer at any time.
brief_signoff.state_drifted: Brief updated since your last sign-off
brief_signoff.drifted_body: Your designer has revised the brief above. Please read the new version and re-sign so we can carry on with the agreed scope on record.
brief_signoff.cannot_sign: Sign-off isn't available from this account.

brief_signoff_staff.title: Customer sign-off
brief_signoff_staff.none_body: The customer hasn't signed off the brief yet. Once they do, the timestamp and a frozen copy of the brief are recorded here as written evidence.
brief_signoff_staff.current_body: The customer signed off the current brief on {date}. This sign-off is the operative agreed brief for the project.
brief_signoff_staff.drifted_body: The customer signed off on {date}, but the brief has been edited since. Their consent no longer matches the live brief — ask them to re-sign before proceeding on the revised scope.

brief_comments.title: Brief discussion
brief_comments.empty: No comments yet. Start the conversation.
brief_comments.new_placeholder: Write a comment. Both Fablab and the customer can see this thread.
brief_comments.confirm_delete: Delete this comment? This can't be undone.
brief_comments.read_only: Comments are read-only for you right now.

clients_page.empty: No clients yet. They're captured when a lead is created.

workshop_page.subtitle: In-house fabrication shops and their live jobs.
workshop_page.empty_body: Add a vendor of kind ‘Internal workshop’ to track in-house fabrication. Once registered it can receive purchase orders like any other vendor.
workshop_page.no_active_jobs: No jobs currently in flight at the workshop.
workshop_page.scope_note_body: Capacity planning, shop-floor scheduling, and per-job throughput live in this module's future iteration. Today the page surfaces what the rest of the system already knows: which vendor rows represent in-house workshops, and which POs are routed to them.
